data.explanation: In a linked list traversal, each step must move the pointer forward by exactly one node using `temp = temp->next`. When you write `temp->next->next`, you skip a node entirely. Worse, if `temp->next` is NULL (e.g., at the last node or when the list has an odd number of nodes), `temp->next->next` dereferences NULL and causes a segmentation fault. The correct approach is to always advance by one node so that every node is visited exactly once.
data.worked_example: Consider the list: 10 -> 20 -> 30 -> NULL. With `temp = temp->next->next`: Start: temp = node(10). Print 10. Then temp = temp->next->next = node(10)->next->next = node(30). Print 30. Then temp = node(30)->next->next = NULL->next → SEGFAULT. The node with data 20 is never visited. With the correct `temp = temp->next`: Start: temp = node(10). Print 10. temp = temp->next = node(20). Print 20. temp = temp->next = node(30). Print 30. temp = temp->next = NULL. Loop ends. Output: 10 20 30. Every node visited.
